SPORTS

OLYMPICS

#### History of Olympics

  • Governing body: International Olympic Committee (IOC) → Conducts Olympics.
  • Headquarters: Initially in Paris, France → Currently in Lausanne, Switzerland.
  • Founded in: 1894 by Pierre de Coubertin (2nd President of IOC) and Demetrius Vikelas (1st President of IOC).
  • Current President of IOC: Thomas Bach.
  • Official motto: "Citius, Altius, Fortius – Communiter" (Faster, Higher, Stronger – Together).
  • Symbol: Olympic Rings (Blue, Yellow, Black, Green, Red) representing the unity of the five continents.
  • Total member countries: 206.
  • Selection of host cities: They are chosen through a Secret Ballot.

#### Olympic Games Timeline

  • First Summer Olympics: 1896 (Athens, Greece).
  • First Winter Olympics: 1924 (Chamonix, France).
  • First Paralympics: 1960 (Rome, Italy).
  • First Youth Summer Olympics: 2010 (Singapore).
  • First Youth Winter Olympics: 2012 (Innsbruck, Austria).
  • Second Olympic Games: 1900 (Paris, France) → First women participation was seen here.
The first Winter Paralympics Games held in Sweden in 1976.
2 years gap between Summer and Winter Olympics.

#### Upcoming Olympics Events

  • 2024 (33rd Edition) Summer Olympics: Paris (France).
  • 2026 Winter Olympics: Milan and Cortina (Italy).
  • 2028 Summer Olympics: Los Angeles, California, USA.
  • 2030 Winter Olympics: French Alps (France).
  • 2032 Summer Olympics: Brisbane (Australia).
  • 2034 Winter Olympics: Salt Lake City (USA).

#### Hosting Cities

  • Most number of times hosted by: USA (8 times → 4 Summer and 4 Winter Olympics).
  • London: 3 times.
  • Paris: 3 times.
  • Los Angeles: 3 times.

INDIA'S PERFORMANCE IN OLYMPICS

  • 1900: First participation of India in Paris, France.
  • First Indian medalist: Norman Pritchard (Anglo-Indians) → won 2 silver medals in 1900.
  • 1920: India's first-ever Olympic contingent, a six-member team participated in Belgium Olympics → First flag bearer: Purma Banerjee.
  • Total medals won by India: 41 medals.
  • 10 Gold medals (8 medals won by Indian Hockey Team and 2 individual medals won) + 10 Silver + 21 Bronze.

In Hockey

  • The Indian Men's Hockey team is the most successful team in Olympics with a record of winning 8 gold + 1 silver + 4 bronze till now.

Participation of Indian Men's Hockey Team

  • 1916: No Olympics held due to World War I (1914-1918).
  • 1928: Amsterdam Olympics → Captain of Indian Men's Hockey Team: Jaipal Singh Munda. 14 goals scored by Major Dhyan Chand (he is considered as "Wizard of Hockey").
  • 1932: Los Angeles Olympics → Won from US by 24-1.
  • 1936: Berlin Olympics (Captain: Dhyan Chand).
  • 1940-1944: No Olympics due to World War II (1939-1945).
  • 1948: London Olympics → Men's Hockey team was led by Kishan Lal.
  • 1952: Helsinki Olympics → Balbir Singh Sr. scored 5 goals (he is the first recipient of Padma Shri award).
  • 1956: Melbourne Olympics → 6th gold medal won.
  • 1960: Rome Olympics → A silver medal won.
  • 1964: Tokyo Olympics → 7th gold medal won by defeating Pakistan. India also won 2 Bronze medals in:
  • 1968: Mexico Olympics → bronze medal won.
  • 1972: Munich Olympics → bronze medal won.
  • 1976: Montreal Olympics → India went home with no medal.
  • 1980: Moscow Olympics → 8th gold medal won.

Individual Gold Medals Won by India in Olympics

  • 2008: Beijing Olympics → Abhinav Bindra in 10 m Air Rifle Shooting.
  • 2020: Tokyo Olympics → Neeraj Chopra was the first Indian to win gold in Track and Field (record: 87.58 m) on 7th August (this day is now celebrated as "National Javelin Day").
Abhinav Bindra is the first Indian to receive the International Shooting Federation (ISSF) Blue Cross.

Some Notable Olympic Medalists of India

  • 1952: Helsinki Olympics → First individual bronze medal won by K.D. Jadhav in Wrestling.
  • 1996: Atlanta Olympics → Leander Paes won bronze medal in Tennis.
  • 2000: Sydney Olympics → Karnam Malleswari became the first woman to win medal (bronze) in Olympics in weightlifting.
  • 2004: Athens Olympics → Silver medal won by Rajvardhan Singh Rathore in shooting (1st Indian to win medal in shooting).
  • 2008: Beijing Olympics → Vijendra Singh won bronze medal in boxing and Sushil Kumar won bronze medal in wrestling.

2012 London Olympics

  • Sushil Kumar: He won a silver in wrestling.
  • Vijay Kumar: He won a silver in shooting.
  • Saina Nehwal: She won a bronze medal and is also the first Indian to win a medal in Badminton.
  • Mary Kom: She won a silver medal and is also the first Indian woman to win a medal in Boxing.
  • Yogeshwar Dutt: He won a bronze medal in wrestling.
  • Gagan Narang: He won a bronze medal in 10m air rifle shooting event.
Beijing is the first city to host both Summer and Winter Olympics editions.

CRICKET

  • Governing body (international cricket): International Cricket Council (ICC). ICC was established as Imperial Cricket Conference in 1909 and became ICC in 1989.
  • Headquarters: Dubai, UAE.
  • Governing body (Indian Cricket): Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI).
  • Headquarters: Mumbai.
  • First Test Match: 1877 (Australia vs England, in England).
  • First ODI Match: 1971 (Australia vs England, Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG)).
Sports Authority of India (SAI) was setup in 1984.

Cricket World Cup

  • First cricket World Cup: Women (1973, in England) and Men (1975, in England) → Winner: West Indies.
  • India has won World Cup two times: 1983 (under Kapil Dev's captaincy) by defeating West Indies and in 2011 (under MS Dhoni's captaincy) by defeating Sri Lanka.
  • 2023 World Cup (held in India): Won by Australia (6th title) by defeating India. Australia holds the record for the most ICC Men's Cricket World Cup titles.

ICC Men's Cricket World Cups Hosted by India

  • 1987: India and Pakistan jointly hosted.
  • 1996: India, Sri Lanka and Pakistan jointly hosted.

Dimensions

  • Cricket field shape: It is generally oval or circular.
  • Weight of cricket ball: 156-163 g.
  • Cricket pitch length: 22 yards. The distance between the stumps and the popping crease at the same end of a cricket pitch is 1.22 m.
  • Wicket (Stump) height: 28 inches.
  • In One Day Internationals (ODIs), a bowler can bowl a maximum of 10 overs, while in T20 matches, the maximum is 4 overs.
  • Ball change is allowed to only after 80 overs.
  • Strike rate calculation: (Total runs scored / Total balls faced) × 100
  • In a test match cricket, a team can play a minimum of 90 overs in a day.
  • Test match per hour is of 15 overs and ODI match is of 50 overs and 3.5 hrs.

Terms Associated

  • "Strike rate" best describes the average number of runs a batter makes per 100 deliveries in cricket.
  • In cricket, if the umpire raises an index finger above the head it means: Batsman is out.
  • In Cricket, if the umpire extends both hands horizontally it means: Wide ball.
  • The first slip fielding position is behind the batsman.
  • The term "Chinaman" in cricket refers to leg-spin delivery by a left-arm bowler.
Nick names of MS Dhoni: "Captain cool", "Thala", "Mahi".

  • Red Card: Fault (opponent is awarded a point).

SPORTS

  • Governing body (India): All India Chess Federation (AICF).
  • Headquarters: New Delhi.

Basic Setup

  • Board Size: 8 × 8 grid = 64 squares (alternating black and white)
  • Each player starts with 16 pieces:
  • 1 King: Moves one square in any direction.
  • 1 Queen: Moves diagonally, horizontally, or vertically.
  • 2 Rook: Moves horizontally or vertically.
  • 2 Bishop: Moves diagonally.
  • 2 Knight: Moves in an 'L-shape'.
  • 8 Pawn: Moves one square forward, but on its first move, it can move two squares forward.

Terms Associated:

  • Stalemate; Checkmate; Gambit, Grandmaster (GM), Castling.

Associated Tournament:

  • R Praggnanandhaa: Young prodigy, reached 2023 FIDE World Cup final.
  • Gukesh D: Among youngest Super Grandmasters, broke into world top 10.
  • Top women players: Koneru Humpy (1st Indian Grandmaster in Women's Chess to become World Rapid Champion); Tania Sachdev; Bhakti Kulkarni; R Vaishali.
  • Magnus Carlsen: Norwegian Chess Grandmaster.
The current World Chess Champion is Gukesh Dommaraju. He won the title by defeating Ding Liren in the 2024 World Chess Championship in Singapore. Gukesh became the youngest World Chess Champion ever at 18 years old.

Factual Verifications

  • IOC: Founded 1894 by Pierre de Coubertin (2nd President) and Demetrius Vikelas (1st President). HQ Lausanne, Switzerland. Motto "Citius, Altius, Fortius – Communiter" (Faster, Higher, Stronger – Together). 206 member countries — verified.
  • Olympic timeline: First Summer 1896 (Athens), first Winter 1924 (Chamonix), first Paralympics 1960 (Rome), first Youth Summer 2010 (Singapore), first Youth Winter 2012 (Innsbruck) — verified.
  • Upcoming: 2024 Paris, 2026 Milan-Cortina, 2028 LA, 2030 French Alps, 2032 Brisbane, 2034 Salt Lake City — verified.
  • 1900 Paris: India's first participation; Norman Pritchard's 2 silver medals — verified (though his Indian identity is debated, it is the accepted SSC/UPSC standard).
  • 2024 Paris Olympics medal tally: 6 medals (1 silver + 5 bronze), rank 71/206, 117 athletes — verified.
  • Manu Bhaker (Women's 10m air pistol, bronze), Manu Bhaker & Sarabjot Singh (Mixed team 10m air pistol, bronze), Swapnil Singh (Men's 50m rifle 3 positions, bronze), Hockey team (bronze), Neeraj Chopra (Men's javelin, silver), Aman Sehrawat (Men's freestyle 57kg, bronze) — all verified.
  • 2024 Paris Paralympics: 7 gold, 9 silver, 13 bronze = 29 medals — verified.
  • Avani Lekhara (Women's 10m air rifle SH1, gold), Nitesh Kumar (Badminton SL3, gold), Sumit Antil (Javelin F64, gold), Harvinder Singh (Recurve open, gold), Dharambir (Club throw F51, gold), Praveen Kumar (High jump T64, gold), Navdeep Singh (Javelin F41, gold) — all verified.
  • Neeraj Chopra Tokyo 2020: 87.58 m gold; first Indian individual Olympic gold in athletics; National Javelin Day 7 Aug — verified.
  • Abhinav Bindra Beijing 2008: First individual Olympic gold for India (10m air rifle) — verified.
  • Hockey: 8 Olympic golds (1928–1980), K. D. Jadhav 1952 bronze (first individual), Major Dhyan Chand "Wizard of Hockey" — verified.
  • IOA: Founded 1927, first President Dorabji Tata, second Maharaja Bhupindra Singh (1928), current President P. T. Usha ("Payyoli Express") — verified.
  • CWG: First 1930 Hamilton; not held 1942 & 1946 (WWII); India hosted 2010; 2022 Birmingham (4th place); Glasgow 2026 (4th time hosting) — verified.
  • Cricket: ICC estd 1909 (Imperial Cricket Conference), HQ Dubai; BCCI HQ Mumbai; first Test 1877 (Aus vs Eng), first ODI 1971 (Aus vs Eng, MCG); 2023 WC won by Australia (6th title); India won 1983 (Kapil Dev) and 2011 (Dhoni) — verified.
  • T20 WC: First 2007 (India won); India also won 2024 (vs South Africa) — verified.
  • Champions Trophy: India 3 titles (current 2025 champions) — verified.
  • FIFA: First 1930 Uruguay; Brazil 5 wins; 2022 winner Argentina (Qatar) — verified.
  • Hockey World Cup: First 1971 (Pakistan won); Pakistan 4 titles; India won 1975 — verified.
  • FIH Hockey5s: First edition 2024 Muscat (Oman); Netherlands won both men & women — verified.
  • Tennis Grand Slams: Wimbledon (1877, grass), US Open (1881, hard), French Open (1891, clay), Australian Open (1905, hard) — verified.
  • Chess: FIDE estd 1924, HQ Lausanne; Gukesh D became World Champion in 2024 (Singapore) defeating Ding Liren, youngest ever at 18 — verified.
  • Michael Phelps: 28 Olympic medals, 23 gold — verified.
  • Wilson Jones: India's first world champion in any sport after independence (Billiards) — verified.
